idiom_name: explicit conversion function over DTO structs with encoding/json struct tags
implementation_notes: Go has neither inheritance nor a reflection-based mapper in the standard library, so the local idiom is one struct per wire contract plus an explicit conversion function (func toCanonical(l legacyOrder) (Order, error)), with field-name differences declared as `json:"..."` struct tags and structural differences handled by MarshalJSON/UnmarshalJSON methods (pkg.go.dev/encoding/json). The classic Translator object collapses into that function; keep it beside the contract it serves and make it total, mapping or deliberately dropping every field. A translator type is still justified when the mapping needs injected collaborators (code-list lookups, a clock) or when one component must serve several wire versions.
pitfalls: json.Unmarshal ignores unknown fields and leaves absent ones at their zero value, so a wrong-shaped message becomes a valid-looking zero struct; decode with DisallowUnknownFields or validate explicitly.
json.Marshal only fails for unsupported types (chan, func) - it will happily emit a translated struct with a nil pointer field as null, so the send path needs its own validation.
A typed nil (a nil *T inside an interface) marshals as null, propagating a translated message whose required field silently disappeared.
